audit.whatIsWrong: The page treats OVERHEATING as his damage spike ('overheated Flamespitter shreds', 'your W heal eats his overheat burst'). Overheating is the state where he CANNOT cast spells. The empowerment threshold is Danger Zone at 50% heat.
audit.why: Junkyard Titan: 'When he reaches 50% Heat he reaches Danger Zone, granting all his basic abilities bonus effects. When he reaches 100% Heat, he starts Overheating, gaining bonus Attack Speed and granting his basic attacks bonus damage, but making him unable to cast spells.' So a full heat bar is your window to walk in, not your cue to back off — the page had the read exactly inverted.
audit.corrected: Back off at 50% heat (Danger Zone); step in at 100% (Overheating) when his abilities are locked out.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers read Rumble / Rumble / Skill x5. The 879-game packet reads Skill / Morde / Morde / Skill / Morde / Morde / Skill on a 54.18% win rate.
audit.why: The page's own whys already match: level 1 'farm even', 2 and 3 yours, whys[3] 'tightens back toward even', whys[4] and whys[5] yours, whys[6] 'a teamfight evens out'.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1, 2, 4 and 5 flipped in BOTH layers as one atomic group -> Skill, Mordekaiser, Mordekaiser, (3 unchanged), Mordekaiser, Mordekaiser, (6 unchanged).

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 and first item were marked Skill despite the page calling them your cleanest kill window and a lethal spike.
audit.why: Realm of Death is 650 range on 140s at rank 1 and leaves his placed Equalizer behind; The Equalizer itself is 130/105/80s at 1750 range, a fight-shaping tool rather than a duel spike.
audit.corrected: Both rows credited to you; his edge is grouped fights only.

audit.whatIsWrong: Electro Harpoon's MAGIC RESIST shred was never mentioned, and neither was The Equalizer cutting off your retreat.
audit.why: Electro Harpoon: 850 range, two stored charges, 0.5s between casts, 'slowing their Move Speed, and reducing their Magic Resist' — it directly undercuts the 'build MR' advice the page opens with. Mordekaiser has no dash, so an Equalizer laid behind him is a wall he cannot cross.
audit.corrected: Harpoon shred stated in whys[3]; Equalizer retreat-cut added to dontsFull[1].d with its 130s cooldown.

edits.before: Rumble has no heat at level 1, so his Flamespitter is just a weak puddle of damage — don't respect it. The moment you hit 2-3 with Q (Obliterate) and W (Indestructible), single-target your Q into him and bank the shield off his ticks; your sustain laughs off un-heated Flamespitter. Watch his heat bar — if it's near the overheat threshold (glowing yellow), step back a beat, because overheated Flamespitter shreds; bait it onto the minions, then walk in once it's spent.
edits.after: Rumble has no heat at level 1, so his Flamespitter is just a weak puddle of damage — don't respect it. The moment you hit 2-3 with Q (Obliterate) and W (Indestructible), single-target your Q into him and bank the shield off his ticks; your sustain laughs off a cold Flamespitter. Watch his heat bar — at 50% he hits Danger Zone and every ability is empowered, so step back a beat; the moment it fills to 100% he Overheats and cannot cast at all, and that is when you walk in.

edits.before: This is your lane. Once Darkness Rise is rolling your extended-trade DPS beats his Flamespitter, and your W heal eats his overheat burst — just don't get caught by his E harpoon-slow and kited out of your aura, so hold your own E (Death's Grasp) to yank him back when he tries to slow-and-run. At 6, R is the trump card: banish him into the shadow realm and his Equalizer zone stays behind on the lane doing nothing, leaving a clean 1v1 where you Q, aura-tick, and W-heal him down.
edits.after: This is your lane. Once Darkness Rise is rolling your extended-trade DPS beats his Flamespitter, and your W heal eats his Danger Zone burst — just don't get caught by his harpoon slow and kited out of your aura, so hold your own E (Death's Grasp) to yank him back when he tries to slow-and-run. At 6, R is the trump card: banish him into the shadow realm and his Equalizer zone stays behind on the lane doing nothing, leaving a clean 1v1 where you Q, aura-tick and W-heal him down.

edits.before: You keep the straight 1v1 all game — your R plus E neutralize his only real edge, which is Equalizer zoning. The danger is that ult in a grouped fight: a well-placed belt zone can chunk your whole team off an objective. So push a sidelane and force him to answer you alone, where you banish him into the shadow realm and delete him before his AOE ever matters. Build a little MR if his overheat burst is scary, but don't over-respect a melee-range AP bruiser you out-sustain.
edits.after: You keep the straight 1v1 all game — your R plus E neutralize his only real edge, which is Equalizer zoning. The danger is that ult in a grouped fight: a well-placed belt zone can chunk your whole team off an objective. So push a sidelane and force him to answer you alone, where you banish him into the shadow realm and delete him before his AOE ever matters. MR helps less than it looks — Electro Harpoon shreds it — so lean on health and your W heal instead.

notes: The most important fix is a reversed read: the page told the player to back off when Rumble's heat bar is full. At 100% heat he is OVERHEATING and cannot cast spells at all — that is the moment to walk in. The threshold that empowers his abilities is Danger Zone at 50%. Also corrected: the page's headline advice is 'build MR', but Electro Harpoon reduces Magic Resist on hit (850 range, two charges), so MR is a soft answer here. suspectNames flagged 'Drop Equalizer' — FALSE POSITIVE, The Equalizer is his real R. Chart disagreed with the 879-game packet in five rows while the whys already read the packet's way; proposed as one atomic paired group. Not asserted (kits do not cover it): whether Overheating also prevents him from recasting Scrap Shield's shield, and whether Realm of Death can be cast onto a target standing in The Equalizer without you entering it.
